scoring: Answer key for comparing Vista (LLM review) with Prowler (rule-based scanner). It holds facts and published AWS Security Hub FSBP control severities only; it contains no ratings of its own. A tool's output is matched to a scenario by the identifier in terraform output scenario_resources (the bucket name). condition flaw: reporting the scenario counts as a detection. condition flaw_blocked: a misconfiguration is present but another deployed control removes the path it opens; reporting it is shown as a separate report rate, counted as neither a detection nor a false positive. condition hardened: no misconfiguration was planted; reporting it is a false positive. fsbp lists the FSBP controls that fail because of the scenario's configuration: a setting in which the scenario differs from its module's hardened default, or a resource its configuration associates with it (none beyond the bucket). fsbp_severity is the highest published severity in that list. On coverage fsbp scenarios the reported severity (NONE when the scenario is not reported) is compared with fsbp_severity on the order NONE < LOW < MEDIUM < HIGH < CRITICAL; outside_fsbp scenarios are scored for detection and false positives only. Controls in baseline_controls fail regardless of scenario and are in no scenario's fsbp. scripts/score.py applies these rules.

baseline_controls.note: FSBP controls known to fail regardless of scenario, for example account-level settings, the VPCs the scenario resources run in, settings left at the module's hardened default that every scenario starts from, and deletion protection, which every resource leaves off so one terraform destroy removes everything. The list is not exhaustive: other FSBP controls can also fail regardless of scenario, depending on account settings at scan time. They are in no scenario's fsbp list. Backing resources no scenario is scored on (for example the S3 access-log bucket, the DynamoDB table, the SQS queue, the KMS key) are not evaluated here.

controls.title: S3 general purpose buckets should have block public access settings enabled
controls.scope: Account setting; account-level Block Public Access cannot be fully on, otherwise the public bucket policies and ACL in s3-02 and s3-04 to s3-08 could not be applied

controls.title: S3 general purpose buckets should have Lifecycle configurations
controls.scope: No Lifecycle configuration on any scenario bucket

scenarios.title: CORS allows any origin to send GET, PUT, and DELETE
scenarios.description: Bucket with the module's hardened settings. Misconfigured: its CORS rule allows origin * to send GET, PUT, and DELETE requests with any header.

scenarios.title: public-read ACL lets anyone list object names
scenarios.description: Bucket with SSE-KMS, versioning, server access logging, a TLS-only policy, and object ownership BucketOwnerPreferred. Misconfigured: the bucket ACL is public-read (an AllUsers READ grant) and its BlockPublicAcls and IgnorePublicAcls settings are off.
scenarios.context: The AllUsers grant is READ on the bucket, which permits listing object keys; neither the grant nor the bucket policy grants reading object data.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket ACL grants AllUsers READ while BlockPublicAcls and IgnorePublicAcls are off

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public access
ACLs should not be used to manage user access to S3 general purpose buckets
fsbp.scope: Bucket ACL (public-read) grants access; object ownership is BucketOwnerPreferred

scenarios.title: Wildcard principal can read and write objects from any account in the organization
scenarios.description: Bucket with the module's hardened settings. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on all objects, with the condition aws:PrincipalOrgID equal to var.org_id.

scenarios.title: Bucket policy allows anonymous s3:GetObject
scenarios.description: Bucket with SSE-KMS, versioning, server access logging, ACLs disabled, and a TLS-only policy. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject on all objects with no condition, and its BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets settings are off.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:GetObject with no condition

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public access

scenarios.title: Bucket policy allows anonymous read, write, and delete
scenarios.description: Bucket with SSE-KMS, versioning, server access logging, ACLs disabled, and a TLS-only policy. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:DeleteObject on all objects with no condition, and its BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets settings are off.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:GetObject with no condition

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public write access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject with no condition

scenarios.title: Static website bucket with anonymous read
scenarios.description: Bucket with static website hosting (index.html, error.html), SSE-S3 (AES256), versioning, server access logging, and ACLs disabled. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject on all objects with no condition, its BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets settings are off, and the policy has no statement denying non-TLS requests.
scenarios.context: Static website hosting is enabled on the bucket; Amazon S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:GetObject with no condition

S3 general purpose buckets should require requests to use TLS

scenarios.title: Anonymous read limited to the public/ prefix
scenarios.description: Bucket with SSE-S3, versioning, server access logging, ACLs disabled, and a TLS-only policy. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject on objects under the public/ prefix with no condition, and its BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets settings are off.
scenarios.context: The anonymous grant covers only objects whose keys begin with public/.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:GetObject on public/* with no condition

scenarios.title: Anonymous read restricted only by aws:Referer
scenarios.description: Bucket with SSE-S3, versioning, server access logging, ACLs disabled, and a TLS-only policy. Misconfigured: its policy allows Principal * to call s3:GetObject on all objects with only an aws:Referer StringLike condition (https://www.<var.name>.example/*, var.name default brightpath), and its BlockPublicPolicy and RestrictPublicBuckets settings are off.

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
fsbp.scope: Bucket policy allows Principal * s3:GetObject with only an aws:Referer StringLike condition, which contains a wildcard; the control does not evaluate conditions that use wildcards

fsbp.title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public access

scenarios.title: Fully hardened application configuration bucket
scenarios.description: Bucket with all four Block Public Access settings on, ACLs disabled (BucketOwnerEnforced), SSE-KMS, versioning, server access logging, and a policy denying non-TLS requests. Hardened: no misconfiguration was planted.

scenarios.title: Fully hardened backup bucket with Object Lock
scenarios.description: Bucket with the same settings as app-config plus Object Lock enabled, with no default retention. Hardened: no misconfiguration was planted.

scenarios.title: Private scratch bucket without versioning or access logging
scenarios.description: Bucket with all four Block Public Access settings on, ACLs disabled, SSE-KMS, and a TLS-only policy. Misconfigured: versioning is not enabled and server access logging is off.
